docs.title: What is Edubadges Server?
docs.text:
Edubadges Server is a Python/Django REST API backend for issuing and managing digital credentials in educational contexts. It follows the Open Badges specification and serves as the backend for the Edubadges platform — a digital badge management system for universities, schools, and educational organizations across the Netherlands and beyond.

The project originated from Badgr, developed by Concentric Sky starting in 2015 as an open-source reference implementation of the Open Badges Specification.

docs.title: Core Purpose
docs.text: Edubadges enables educational institutions to: - Create, issue, and manage digital badges following the Open Badges standard - Support micro-credentials — certification units smaller than a full diploma - Integrate with learning management systems via LTI 1.3 - Provide multi-provider SSO (eduID, SURFConext) for Dutch higher education - Issue verifiable credentials following the W3C Open Badges 3 specification

docs.title: Target Users
docs.text: Role Description Educational Institutions Universities and schools managing badge programs Students & Learners Recipients of badges (badge earners) Instructors & Administrators Creators and issuers of badges HR Departments Organizations recognizing skills and achievements

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Badge Issuance: Full badge lifecycle management — create, issue, revoke, and verify digital badges
  • Badge Management: Comprehensive tools for issuers to manage their badge classes and assertions
  • User Management: Support for badge earners, issuers, and institutional administrators with role-based access control
  • LTI Integration: LTI 1.3 deep linking for learning management system integration (Canvas, etc.)
  • Multi-Provider SSO: eduID and SURFConext authentication for Dutch higher education
  • Micro-credentials: Support for smaller certification units beyond full diplomas
  • Verifiable Credentials: Open Badges 3 (W3C) integration with blockchain timestamping
  • Direct Awards: Bulk badge issuance via SIS integration with scheduled awards
  • Public Verification: JSON-LD endpoints for Open Badges spec compliance and badge verification
  • Mobile API: Dedicated endpoints for the mobile companion app
  • Analytics: Insights and query endpoints for badge program analytics
  • Institutional Hierarchy: Institution → Faculty → Issuer organizational structure with cascading permissions

git clone https://github.com/edubadges/edubadges-server.git
cd edubadges-server

docs.title: Architecture Summary
docs.text:
The system follows a layered Django architecture with 30+ applications organized into functional domains:

  1. Core Infrastructure — mainsite, badgeuser, basic_models, cachemodel, entity
  2. Badge Domain — issuer, signing, endorsement, directaward, backpack
  3. Institutional Hierarchy — institution, staff
  4. Integration — lti13, lti_edu, badgrsocialauth, ob3
  5. API Layers — mobile_api, public, badge_connect, insights, queries
  6. Support — notifications, theming, badgrlog, health

See 2. Architecture Overview.md for detailed architecture diagrams.

docs.title: 1. Entity-ID Based Routing
docs.text: Every major entity uses a UUID-based entity_id for URL routing and JSON-LD @id fields, enabling: - Stable, opaque identifiers across all APIs - JSON-LD @id compliance with Open Badges specification - Decoupled URLs from database primary keys

docs.title: 2. Hierarchical Permission System
docs.text:
RBAC via PermissionedRelationshipBase with cascading permissions:

Institution (admin)
  └── Faculty (staff)
      └── Issuer (staff)
          └── BadgeClass (staff)
              └── BadgeInstance (awarded)

Seven permission types cascade down the hierarchy: - may_create — create child entities - may_read — read entities - may_update — update entities - may_delete — delete entities - may_award — award badges - may_sign — sign/cryptographically prove badges - may_administrate_users — manage staff membership

docs.title: 3. Three-Layer API Strategy
docs.text: Layer Technology Purpose REST API DRF ViewSets CRUD operations, versioned (v1, v2) GraphQL API Graphene-Django Complex queries, aggregations Public JSON-LD Custom views Open Badges spec compliance, verification

docs.title: 4. Caching Layer
docs.text: Custom CacheModel base class with @cached_method decorator provides: - Automatic method-level caching with cache invalidation on save/delete - Per-model cache keys based on entity_id - Memcached-backed storage via pymemcache

docs.title: 5. Badge Instance (Assertion) Lifecycle
docs.text:
Created → Submitted for Timestamping → Signed → Awarded → [Revoked]
Each badge instance progresses through cryptographic signing with timestamp proofs anchored to the BTC ledger.

docs.title: 6. Environment-Driven Configuration
docs.text: All configuration is environment-variable driven via env_vars.sh. No hardcoded secrets. Docker Compose for local development.

docs.title: 7. Multi-Language Support
docs.text: Dutch/English bilingual content for Institutions, Faculties, Issuers, and BadgeClasses: - name_english / name_dutch - description_english / description_dutch - criteria_english / criteria_dutch

docs.title: 1. Entity-ID Over Primary Key
docs.text:
• Decision: Use UUID entity_id for all external references instead of database PKs
  • Rationale: Stable identifiers across migrations, JSON-LD compliance, opaque URLs
  • Trade-off: Slightly larger indices, but better security and portability

docs.title: 2. Hybrid API Strategy (REST + GraphQL + JSON-LD)
docs.text:
• Decision: Three parallel API strategies for different consumers
  • Rationale: REST for CRUD, GraphQL for complex queries, JSON-LD for Open Badges spec compliance
  • Trade-off: Higher development/maintenance cost, but serves all consumer needs optimally

docs.title: 3. Hierarchical RBAC with Cascading Permissions
docs.text:
• Decision: Institution → Faculty → Issuer → BadgeClass permission cascading
  • Rationale: Mirrors real organizational structures in education
  • Trade-off: Complex permission resolution, but matches domain requirements

docs.title: 4. Environment-Driven Configuration
docs.text:
• Decision: All configuration via environment variables
  • Rationale: Security (no secrets in code), deployment flexibility, Docker-native
  • Trade-off: Requires careful environment setup for new developers

docs.title: 5. Django Monolith with Modular Apps
docs.text:
• Decision: Single Django project with 30+ loosely coupled apps
  • Rationale: Shared database, simple deployment, clear app boundaries
  • Trade-off: Database coupling between apps, but enables cross-domain queries

docs.title: Workflow 1: Badge Creation and Issuance
docs.text:
This is the primary user journey: an instructor creates a badge class and awards it to students.

sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant UI
  participant REST
  participant IssuerSvc
  participant SignSvc
  participant MySQL
  participant FCM

  User->>UI: Create badge class
  UI->>REST: POST /issuer/badge-classes/
  REST->>MySQL: INSERT BadgeClass
  REST-->>UI: BadgeClass created

  User->>UI: Award badge to student
  UI->>REST: POST /issuer/badge-instances/
  REST->>MySQL: INSERT BadgeInstance
  REST-->>UI: BadgeInstance created

  Note over SignSvc: Background task triggers
  SignSvc->>MySQL: SELECT BadgeInstance
  SignSvc->>SignSvc: Sign with PrivateKey
  SignSvc->>MySQL: UPDATE BadgeInstance (signed)
  SignSvc->>FCM: Send push notification
  FCM-->>User: "Badge awarded!"

Steps: 1. Instructor creates a BadgeClass with name, description, criteria, and image 2. BadgeClass is validated against Open Badges schema 3. Instructor awards BadgeInstance (assertion) to a BadgeUser 4. Background task submits instance for cryptographic timestamping 5. SigningService signs the assertion with institutional private key 6. Timestamp proof is optionally anchored to BTC ledger 7. User receives push notification via Firebase Cloud Messaging 8. Badge is available in the user's backpack and publicly verifiable

docs.title: Workflow 2: Direct Award (Bulk Issuance)
docs.text:
Bulk badge issuance for SIS integration or class-wide awards.

sequenceDiagram
  participant Admin
  participant REST
  participant DirectAward
  participant Celery
  participant BadgeInstance
  participant Email
  participant FCM

  Admin->>REST: Create DirectAwardBundle
  REST->>DirectAward: INSERT DirectAward
  Admin->>REST: Assign users (EPPN/email list)
  DirectAward->>Celery: Queue scheduled awards

  Note over Celery: Scheduled time arrives
  Celery->>DirectAward: Process bundle
  DirectAward->>BadgeInstance: CREATE for each user
  BadgeInstance->>Email: Send notification email
  BadgeInstance->>FCM: Send push notification

  Celery->>DirectAward: Audit trail
  DirectAward->>MySQL: INSERT DirectAwardAuditTrail

Steps: 1. Administrator creates a DirectAwardBundle referencing a BadgeClass 2. Users are identified by EPPN (eduID) or email address 3. Bundle is scheduled for future processing (or immediate) 4. Celery worker processes the bundle at scheduled time 5. BadgeInstance records are created for each matching user 6. Audit trail is recorded for compliance 7. Affected users receive email and push notifications

docs.title: Workflow 3: LTI 1.3 Integration
docs.text:
Learning Management System integration for launching Edubadges as an LTI tool.

sequenceDiagram
  participant LMS
  participant Browser
  participant Edubadges
  participant LTI13
  participant Auth

  LMS->>Browser: Launch LTI tool (deep link)
  Browser->>Edubadges: /lti/deep_linking/
  Edubadges->>LTI13: Parse LTI message
  LTI13->>Auth: Validate JWT (OIDC)
  Auth-->>LTI13: Valid
  LTI13->>Edubadges: Launch with context
  Edubadges-->>Browser: LTI frame with badge picker
  Browser->>Edubadges: Select badges (deep link return)
  Edubadges->>LMS: Return LTI Deep Linking payload
  LMS->>LMS: Embed badges in course

Steps: 1. Instructor launches Edubadges from within an LMS (Canvas, Moodle) via LTI 1.3 2. OIDC authentication validates the LTI message 3. Edubadges presents badge picker within LMS iframe 4. Instructor selects badges to embed in course 5. Edubadges returns Deep Linking payload to LMS 6. LMS embeds selected badges in course content

docs.title: Workflow 4: Badge Verification (Public JSON-LD)
docs.text:
Third-party verification of badge assertions via the public API.

sequenceDiagram
  participant Verifier
  participant PublicAPI
  participant MySQL
  participant SignSvc

  Verifier->>PublicAPI: GET /public/assertions/<entity_id>
  PublicAPI->>MySQL: SELECT BadgeInstance
  MySQL-->>PublicAPI: BadgeInstance data
  PublicAPI->>SignSvc: Verify cryptographic signature
  SignSvc->>MySQL: SELECT PublicKey
  MySQL-->>SignSvc: Public key
  SignSvc-->>PublicAPI: Signature valid
  PublicAPI-->>Verifier: JSON-LD badge assertion

Steps: 1. Third-party verifier requests badge assertion via public JSON-LD endpoint 2. Server retrieves BadgeInstance and serializes to JSON-LD per Open Badges spec 3. Cryptographic signature is verified using the associated public key 4. JSON-LD response includes all required Open Badges fields 5. Verifier validates the @context, @id, and cryptographic proof

docs.title: Workflow 5: Social Authentication (eduID/SURFConext)
docs.text:
Multi-provider SSO for Dutch higher education users.

sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant UI
  participant Edubadges
  participant AllAuth
  participant eduID
  participant BadgeUser

  User->>UI: Click "Login with eduID"
  UI->>Edubadges: /accounts/eduid/login/
  Edubadges->>AllAuth: Redirect to eduID
  AllAuth->>eduID: OIDC authorization request
  eduID-->>User: Login page
  User->>eduID: Enter credentials
  eduID-->>AllAuth: Authorization code
  AllAuth->>eduID: Exchange code for token
  eduID-->>AllAuth: ID token + user info
  AllAuth->>BadgeUser: Create/find BadgeUser
  BadgeUser-->>AllAuth: User object
  AllAuth-->>UI: Login successful
  UI-->>User: Dashboard

Steps: 1. User clicks SSO provider button (eduID or SURFConext) 2. Django Allauth redirects to provider's OIDC endpoint 3. User authenticates with institutional credentials 4. Authorization code is exchanged for ID token 5. User info is extracted (EPPN, schacHomeOrganization, etc.) 6. BadgeUser is created or looked up by email 7. User is logged in and redirected to the application

docs.title: Issuer Model
docs.text:
Represents an educational organization that issues badges.

class Issuer(
    EntityUserProvisionmentMixin, ArchiveMixin, PermissionedModelMixin,
    ImageUrlGetterMixin, BaseAuditedModel, DefaultLanguageMixin,
    BaseVersionedEntity, BaseOpenBadgeObjectModel,
):
    # Bilingual fields
    name_english = models.CharField(max_length=512)
    name_dutch = models.CharField(max_length=512)
    description_english = models.TextField()
    description_dutch = models.TextField()

    # Organization hierarchy
    faculty = models.ForeignKey('institution.Faculty', on_delete=models.CASCADE)

    # Staff and permissions
    staff = models.ManyToManyField('badgeuser.BadgeUser', through='staff.IssuerStaff')

    # Image and contact
    image_english = models.FileField(upload_to='uploads/issuers')
    image_dutch = models.FileField(upload_to='uploads/issuers')
    email = models.CharField(max_length=254)

Key behaviors: - Bilingual fallback: name property returns English or Dutch based on language context - Image inheritance: Falls back to faculty image, then institution image - Unique validation: Prevents duplicate names within same faculty - Archival: Can be archived if no active badge instances reference it - Reporting: get_report() aggregates assertion counts by type

docs.text:
Defines a badge type — the "template" for assertions.

class BadgeClass(
    EntityUserProvisionmentMixin, PermissionedModelMixin,
    ImageUrlGetterMixin, DefaultLanguageMixin,
    BaseVersionedEntity, BaseOpenBadgeObjectModel,
):
    issuer = models.ForeignKey(Issuer, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    name_english = models.CharField(max_length=512)
    name_dutch = models.CharField(max_length=512)

    description_dutch = models.TextField()
    criteria_english = models.TextField()  # Requirements to earn
    criteria_dutch = models.TextField()

    formal = models.BooleanField(default=False)  # formal vs informal credential
    tags = models.ManyToManyField('institution.BadgeClassTag')
    award_allowed_institutions = models.ManyToManyField('institution.Institution')

Key behaviors: - Formal vs Informal: Tracks whether a badge is part of a formal curriculum - Criteria: Stores requirements as human-readable text (Open Badges criteria field) - Institution restrictions: Optional list of institutions allowed to award this badge - Tagging: Categorical tags for classification and filtering - Assertions count: Cached count of issued instances

docs.text:
Represents a single awarded badge to a specific user.

class BadgeInstance(
    PermissionedModelMixin, ArchiveMixin,
    DefaultLanguageMixin, BaseVersionedEntity,
    BaseOpenBadgeObjectModel,
):
    badgeclass = models.ForeignKey(BadgeClass, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    issuer = models.ForeignKey(Issuer, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    user = models.ForeignKey('badgeuser.BadgeUser', on_delete=models.CASCADE, null=True)
    issued_nano = models.BigIntegerField()  # Nanosecond-precision timestamp
    revoked = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    revocation_reason = models.CharField(max_length=1024, blank=True)
    public_key_issuer = models.ForeignKey(PublicKeyIssuer, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    direct_award_bundle = models.ForeignKey(DirectAwardBundle, on_delete=models.PROTECT, null=True)
    assertion_json = JSONField(default=dict)  # Signed assertion payload

Key behaviors: - Nanosecond precision: issued_nano stores nanosecond-precision timestamps per Open Badges spec - Revocation: Supports revocation with optional reason (visible in JSON-LD) - Cryptographic signing: Each assertion is signed with a PublicKeyIssuer key - Evidence: Linked BadgeInstanceEvidence records for supporting materials - Direct award tracking: Links to DirectAwardBundle if awarded via bulk process - Assertion JSON: Contains the full signed assertion payload

docs.title: Potential Improvements
docs.text:
1. BadgeInstance state machine: Current state tracking is implicit (signed, revoked). A proper state machine would make transitions explicit and auditable.

  2. BadgeClass versioning: BadgeClass supports OBI versioning at the entity level, but changes to criteria/description are not versioned. Consider a BadgeClassVersion model for audit trails.

  3. Evidence file storage: Currently stored in local uploads/evidence. Consider S3-compatible storage for production deployments.

  4. Async evidence upload: Large evidence files are uploaded synchronously. Consider chunked uploads with background processing.

  5. BadgeClass templates: No built-in template system for creating similar badge classes. Could benefit from a clone/template feature.

  6. Bulk badge export: No built-in export of badge data to CSV/JSON. Useful for institutional reporting.

docs.title: CacheModel Base Class
docs.text:
class CacheModel(models.Model):
    """Base model with automatic caching."""
    class Meta:
        abstract = True

    @classmethod
    def get_cache_key(cls, instance):
        """Generate cache key for an instance."""
        return f'{cls.__name__}_{instance.entity_id}'

    @classmethod
    def get_from_cache(cls, instance):
        """Get instance from cache."""
        key = cls.get_cache_key(instance)
        return memcached.get(key)

    @classmethod
    def invalidate_cache(cls, instance):
        """Invalidate cache for an instance."""
        key = cls.get_cache_key(instance)
        memcached.delete(key)

docs.title: @cached_method Decorator
docs.text:
from cachemodel.decorators import cached_method

class Issuer(...):
    @cached_method(auto_publish=True)
    def cached_badgeclasses(self):
        """Cached method that invalidates on save/delete."""
        return list(self.badgeclasses.all())

    @cached_method(auto_publish=True)
    def cached_staff(self):
        return list(IssuerStaff.objects.filter(issuer=self))

The decorator: 1. Caches the method result in Memcached 2. Automatically invalidates on model save/delete (when auto_publish=True) 3. Uses entity_id-based cache keys for consistency

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
1. Private Key Storage: Private keys are stored in the database as binary fields. In production, consider HSM or cloud KMS integration.

  2. Key Rotation: No automated key rotation. When a key pair is compromised or expires, a new PublicKeyIssuer must be created manually.

  3. Access Control: Key management should be restricted to administrators. The current RBAC system provides institutional-level access.

  4. Backup: Private keys must be backed up separately from the database. Loss of private keys means inability to sign new assertions (though existing signatures remain valid).

docs.title: Potential Improvements
docs.text:
1. Automated Key Rotation: Implement automatic key pair rotation with overlap period for seamless transition.

  2. HSM Integration: Support for hardware security modules (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) for private key storage.

  3. Multiple Active Keys: Allow multiple active key pairs per institution for gradual key rotation without breaking existing assertions.

  4. Key Expiry Dates: Add expires_at field to PublicKeyIssuer with automatic deprecation warnings.

  5. Signature Verification Endpoint: Public API endpoint for verifying assertion signatures, useful for third-party integrations.

  6. Ledger Agnostic: Currently tied to BTC ledger. Consider abstracting to support other blockchains (Ethereum, Polygon).

docs.title: PermissionedModelMixin
docs.text:
All domain models that need permission checking inherit this mixin:

class PermissionedModelMixin:
    def has_permissions(self, user, permissions):
        """Check if user has all specified permissions at this level or parent levels."""
        # Check BadgeClassStaff → IssuerStaff → FacultyStaff → InstitutionStaff
        staff_classes = [
            ('badgeclass', BadgeClassStaff),
            ('issuer', IssuerStaff),
            ('faculty', FacultyStaff),
            ('institution', InstitutionStaff),
        ]

        for field_name, staff_class in staff_classes:
            if hasattr(self, field_name):
                parent = getattr(self, field_name)
                if hasattr(parent, 'staff'):
                    membership = parent.staff.filter(user=user).first()
                    if membership and all(
                        getattr(membership, perm, False) for perm in permissions
                    ):
                        return True
        return False

def match_user(identifier_type, identifier_value):
    """Find a BadgeUser by their identifier."""
    if identifier_type == 'eppn':
        # Match via StudentAffiliation.eppn
        affiliation = StudentAffiliation.objects.filter(eppn=identifier_value).first()

    elif identifier_type == 'email':

The issuer.utils module handles JSON-LD serialization:

from issuer.utils import get_obi_context, CURRENT_OBI_VERSION

def get_json_ld_for_assertion(badgeinstance):
    """Serialize a BadgeInstance to Open Badges JSON-LD."""
    context = get_obi_context(badgeinstance.obi_version)

    data = {
        '@context': context,
        '@type': 'BadgeAssertion',
        '@id': f'{settings.DEFAULT_DOMAIN}/public/assertions/{badgeinstance.entity_id}',
        'id': f'{settings.DEFAULT_DOMAIN}/public/assertions/{badgeinstance.entity_id}',
        'name': f'{badgeinstance.user.validated_name} - {badgeinstance.badgeclass.name}',
        'achievement': {
            '@type': 'BadgeClass',
            'id': f'{settings.DEFAULT_DOMAIN}/public/badges/{badgeinstance.badgeclass.entity_id}',
            'name': badgeinstance.badgeclass.name,
            'description': badgeinstance.badgeclass.description,
            'criteria': {
                'narrative': badgeinstance.badgeclass.criteria,
                'href': badgeinstance.badgeclass.criteria_url,
            },
        },
        'issuer': {...},  # Issuer JSON-LD
        'recipient': {...},  # Hashed recipient identity
        'issuanceDate': badgeinstance.issued_nano,
        'verification': {...},  # Cryptographic verification
        'evidence': [...],  # Evidence URLs
    }

    if badgeinstance.revoked:
        data['verification'] = {
            '@type': 'VerifiableCredential',
            'type': ['Revoked'],
        }

    return data

docs.text:
def verify_assertion(badgeinstance):
    """Verify the cryptographic signature of an assertion."""
    public_key_issuer = badgeinstance.public_key_issuer
    public_key = public_key_issuer.public_key

    # Get the signed assertion JSON
    assertion_json = badgeinstance.assertion_json

    # Verify signature using the public key
    is_valid = public_key.verify(
        assertion_json['signature'],
        assertion_json['signed_data']
    )

    # Check timestamp proof
    timestamp = badgeinstance.timestamp
    if timestamp:
        timestamp_valid = verify_timestamp_proof(
            timestamp.timestamp_proof,
            timestamp.timestamp
        )

    return {
        'valid': is_valid and timestamp_valid,
        'revoked': badgeinstance.revoked,
        'issuer': public_key_issuer.name,
        'blockchain_txid': timestamp.blockchain_txid if timestamp else None,
    }

class MobileAPIAuthentication(BaseAuthentication):
    """Custom authentication for mobile app API calls."""

    def authenticate(self, request):
        # Extract token from Authorization header or query param
        token = request.GET.get('token') or request.META.get('HTTP_AUTHORIZATION')

        if not token:
            return None

        # Validate token and return BadgeUser
        try:
            user = BadgeUser.objects.get(auth_token=token)
            return (user, None)
        except BadgeUser.DoesNotExist:
            return None

class MobileLoginView(APIView):
    """Handle mobile app login."""
    serializer_class = MobileLoginSerializer

    def post(self, request):
        serializer = self.serializer_class(data=request.data)
        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)

        email = serializer.validated_data['email']
        password = serializer.validated_data['password']

        user = authenticate(username=email, password=password)
        if user is None:

        return Response({
            'user_id': user.entity_id,
            'token': token,

class AcceptDirectAwardView(generics.GenericAPIView):
    """Accept a pending direct award."""
    serializer_class = AcceptDirectAwardSerializer
    authentication_classes = [MobileAPIAuthentication]

    def post(self, request, entity_id):
        award = get_object_or_404(DirectAward, entity_id=entity_id)

        # Verify this award belongs to the current user
        if award.identifier_value != request.user.email:
            return Response({'error': 'Not your award'}, status=403)

        # Create the badge instance
        badgeinstance = BadgeInstance.objects.create(
            badgeclass=award.badgeclass,
            issuer=award.badgeclass.issuer,
            user=request.user,
            issued_nano=int(time.time() * 1e9),
        )

        # Mark award as processed
        award.status = 'awarded'
        award.matched_user = request.user
        award.created_instance = badgeinstance
        award.save()

        # Send push notification
        send_push_notification(
            user=request.user,
            title='Badge Awarded!',
            body=f'You received {award.badgeclass.name}',
            data={'badge_instance_id': badgeinstance.entity_id},
        )
